title: Three Haunted Stories from LaPorte County

county historian Fern Eddy Schultz: the former George Andrew home on I Street 'remains the granddaddy for local ghost stories'; the Robert Zimmermann family (1958-63) heard coins drop, and a daughter saw a woman in Victorian clothing appear in an upper window; when the house was razed and the I Street Clinic erected, employees reported flickering lights, flushing toilets, drawers and doors opening and closing by themselves, and disappearing medical instruments
sources.who: What's New LaPorte, 'Look no further than LaPorte for plenty of great ghost stories' (Oct. 25, 2009)

sources.what: mansion at I and 10th Streets gave way in the 1970s to a medical clinic; Zimmermanns 1953-1963; a woman in an 1800s-style dress sighted in the attic dormer window; Schultz a 'non-believer'; nurse friend says instruments laid out disappeared
sources.who: Newspaper feature (NWI Times, 2011) reposted on CityByTheLake.org

sources.what: clinic staff report doors being slammed by an unseen force
Fern Eddy Schultz, LaPorte County historian nearly 30 years, retired end of 2020, died March 2021

Cathcart, judge and ex-congressman turned spiritualist; originally a skeptic, attended his first spirit circle at the home of Mr. Poston of La Porte County to expose fraud; brought a homemade flash device; a spirit called 'old king' took up a bass drum; his Spiritual Telegraph account: '[I] witnessed the stick beating the drum as if handled from above, and no mortal nearer than about eight feet of it!'; became a convert and started his own spirit circle in LaPorte County
sources.who: Indiana Historical Bureau, Talking Hoosier History, 'Spiritualism: Beyond the Spectacle' (2019)

sources.what: Emma Hardinge's history describes a spirit room of the Poston circle in Indiana and Charles Cathcart's spirit room in the same state

beats.text: Three stories from LaPorte County. A chapel that burned, a house that came down, and a congressman who went to a seance to expose it.
beats.label: LAPORTE COUNTY, INDIANA

beats.text: Lights drifting between the graves, on a hill northeast of LaPorte, near Hesston. This is Posey Chapel Cemetery.
beats.label: NEAR HESSTON, LAPORTE COUNTY
beats.credit: Visitor reports: Ghost Research Society · AI-generated picture

beats.text: In 1841, settlers from the surrounding farms built a log chapel here. Local history says it was the first church in Galena Township.
beats.credit: A Century with Posey Chapel (1933) · AI-generated picture

beats.text: They named it for the circuit preacher who urged them to build it, Wade Posey. In 1855, a new chapel replaced the log one.
beats.label: 1855: A NEW CHAPEL
beats.credit: A Century with Posey Chapel (1933) · AI-generated picture

beats.text: It stood for more than a century. Then, on the night of January 26, 1972, arsonists set it on fire, and it burned to the ground.
beats.label: THE FIRE
beats.credit: A Century with Posey Chapel · AI-generated picture

beats.text: Today, a pavilion stands where the chapel was.
beats.label: THE PAVILION

beats.text: Visitors report glowing lights among the stones, and sounds they can't explain.
beats.label: WHAT VISITORS SAY
beats.credit: Visitor reports: Ghost Research Society · AI-generated picture

beats.text: It's a real cemetery. Please visit in daylight, and be respectful.
beats.label: PLEASE BE RESPECTFUL

beats.text: A woman in old-fashioned clothes, looking down from an upper window of a house on I Street in LaPorte.
beats.label: I STREET, LAPORTE

beats.text: The late county historian Fern Eddy Schultz called it the granddaddy of local ghost stories.
beats.label: THE GRANDDADDY
beats.credit: Fern Eddy Schultz, via What's New LaPorte (2009) · AI-generated picture

beats.text: Around 1960, a family living there said a woman in old-fashioned clothes appeared in an upper window.
beats.label: THE UPPER WINDOW

beats.text: Later, the house came down, and a medical clinic now stands on the site.
beats.label: THE CLINIC

beats.text: Then the staff stories started. Instruments laid out for patients would disappear.
beats.label: WHAT STAFF SAID

beats.text: Workers also reported doors opening and closing on their own.
beats.label: DOORS ON THEIR OWN

beats.text: Schultz collected stories like these for years, and told them at the county museum.
beats.label: THE STORYTELLER

beats.text: In the dark, a drum began to beat. And a former congressman from LaPorte had come to prove it was a trick.
beats.label: LAPORTE COUNTY, THE 1800s

beats.text: His name was Charles Cathcart. He farmed near LaPorte, served in Congress, and briefly in the United States Senate.
beats.label: CHARLES CATHCART
beats.credit: Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress · AI-generated picture

beats.text: He didn't believe in spirit circles. So he went to one at the Poston home, to expose it.
beats.label: A LAPORTE COUNTY HOME

beats.text: He brought a homemade device that could light the dark room in a flash.
beats.label: HIS TRAP

beats.text: The lights went out. A spirit the circle called Old King began to beat a bass drum.
beats.label: OLD KING

beats.text: Cathcart hit his light. He wrote that the stick beat the drum as if from above, with no one within about eight feet.
beats.label: WHAT HE WROTE

lines: ...the stick beating the drum as if handled from above,
and no mortal nearer than about eight feet of it!

beats.credit: His account in the Spiritual Telegraph, via Indiana Historical Bureau

beats.text: The skeptic became a believer, and started a spirit circle of his own.
beats.label: CATHCART'S SPIRIT ROOM

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
